validity.recommendation: No change needed to existence/classification/ownership; keep as operating cross-border gas trunk line.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real and well-documented, confirmed by THREE independent, verified sources naming this exact pipeline: (1) GAZ-SYSTEM's (Polish TSO) own press release on a September 2016 gas-pipeline incident, which explicitly describes 'a gas pipeline with a diameter of 800 mm located near Komarno Gas compression station in the Ukrainian Lviv region'; (2) eegas.com's technical table (already cited on the gem.wiki page, cite_note-cap-1) lists a distinct row 'Komarno-Drozdowichi | 5 [bcm/yr] | 2 [lines] | (Drozdowichi)'; (3) Interfax.ru (2022-02-07), reporting on Polish gas sourcing, states verbatim 'удвоились поставки через украину по газопроводу «Комарно-Дроздовичи»' (deliveries via the 'Komarno-Drozdovychi' pipeline doubled to ~8 million cu.m/day in Feb 2022), confirming the pipeline is actively flowing gas. A further Ukrainian-language web search also surfaces a 'Magistralnyi gazoprovid Komarno-Sambir-Drozdovychi' trunk line passing the Rudky gas field, and a CEEnergynews (2020-06-09) piece plus tsoua.com's own news item ('Technical measures on Komarno-Drozdovychi pipeline will not affect gas transit...') show the pipeline is still a live operational/maintenance topic. This is NOT a GEM-only entity. CLASSIFICATION: correctly a gas transmission trunk/interconnector pipeline (not gathering/feeder) — it is explicitly the Ukraine-side leg of the Drozdowicze/Hermanowice cross-border interconnection point with Poland's GAZ-SYSTEM (unified into the single virtual IP 'GCP GAZ-SYSTEM/UA TSO' on 2020-07-01 per CEEnergynews and tsoua.com news). No commodity/type misclassification found. DUPLICATE CHECK: cross-checked against the 39-row Ukraine-gas roster — no match; the closest name collision risk is the separate GEM entity 'Poland-Ukraine Interconnector Gas Pipeline' (gem.wiki), but that page describes a DIFFERENT, cancelled, NEW-build project (Hermanowice, Poland → Bilche-Volytsia UGS, Ukraine; 100 km total, 700/1000 mm, cost €365 million, planned start 2022, operators GAZ-SYSTEM + Ukrtransgaz) — different endpoints, different diameter, different status (cancelled vs operating), and not in the 39-row roster at all. P0778 is not a duplicate of it. ATTRIBUTION (owner/operator): sheet records Owner1 = 'Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine' at 100%, which is correct per country guidance — confirmed via tsoua.com's own 'Key Facts' page (archived, live site 403s bots): 'Starting from January 1, 2020, LLC Gas TSO of Ukraine is the certified operator of the gas transmission system of Ukraine and fully independent of vertically integrated undertakings' and 'October 27, 2023 – ... 100% of the GTSOU's equity stake was transferred to the Ministry of Energy of Ukraine.' CEEnergynews (2020) independently corroborates by naming 'the Ukrainian Gas TSO' as GAZ-SYSTEM's counterparty for exactly this interconnection point. No Gazprom/Ukrtransgaz misattribution found on this row.

validity.recommendation: Route to Update: verify Capacity — independent sources put the two-line Komarno-Drozdovychi system at ~5 bcm/y, not the sheet's 8.00 bcm/y. Do not paste 5 over 8 without further digging; determine whether 8.00 reflects a post-2022-reconstruction increase.
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet records Capacity = 8.00 bcm/y with NO ref. The gem.wiki page itself flags disagreement in its own citations ('Reports vary between 5, 6.6, and 8 bcm/y'), and independent checking supports the LOW end, not the sheet's value: eegas.com's engineering table (already cited on the wiki page) gives 'Komarno-Drozdowichi | 5 [bcm/yr] | 2 [lines]'. Ukrainian Wikipedia's dedicated article on the Komarno–Yaroslav gas-transport corridor independently states the two parallel lines 'Komarno — Drozdovychi — Derzhkordon' have a combined throughput of approximately 5 billion m3/year ('дві нитки Комарно — Дроздовичі — Держкордон ... біля 5 млрд.'). That is two independent sources agreeing on ~5 bcm/y, against zero independent sources found that confirm 8.00 bcm/y as a rated capacity (the Interfax.ru '8 million m3/day' figure is an actual 2022 FLOW/utilization figure, not a rated annual capacity, and even annualized (~2.9 bcm/y) it does not match either 8.00 or 5). I did NOT propose a ref for Capacity because no source I verified actually agrees with the sheet's 8.00 value — filling it with a source that says 5 would create a value/ref mismatch. This is a genuine material spec disagreement per the corroboration standard, not a rubber-stamp UNRESOLVED.

validity.recommendation: No value change recommended for Diameter or Length, but flag for awareness: older Ukrainian/Soviet-era technical literature describes this corridor as TWO separate lines of different vintage/diameter, not one 800mm line.
validity.researcher_notes: DIAMETER: sheet's 800mm is independently and explicitly corroborated by GAZ-SYSTEM's 2016 press release ('a gas pipeline with a diameter of 800 mm located near Komarno Gas compression station'). However, Ukrainian Wikipedia's Komarno–Yaroslav corridor article describes the historical Soviet-era build as TWO separate lines feeding the same border crossing: a 1961 line (78.3 km, 530mm) and a 1975 parallel line (78.4 km, 720mm), plus a short 1966 connector Khidnovychi-Drozdovychi-Derzhkordon (7.9 km, 530mm) — none of which is 800mm. This is not necessarily a contradiction: gem.wiki's own page notes '2022: reconstruction works replacing 100% of the pipeline completed,' so the 800mm figure may reflect the post-2022-rebuilt pipe rather than the original 1960s-70s line(s) the Ukrainian source describes; GAZ-SYSTEM's statement is also from Jan 2016, i.e. before the cited 2022 rebuild, so if accurate it implies 800mm predates that reconstruction too — the record is not fully clean, but the single most specific, English, first-party, verified source matches the sheet value, so I'm not recommending a change, just flagging the historical-diameter discrepancy for anyone digging further into this corridor's segment history. LENGTH: sheet's 80.00 km is in the right neighborhood of the 1961/1975 lines (78.3 / 78.4 km each) but does not exactly match either, and no independent source states exactly '80 km' for this pipeline as GEM defines its endpoints (Komarno CS → Drozdovychi GMS) — the ~1.6–1.7 km gap is plausibly a route/endpoint-definition difference (compressor/metering-station centroids vs the state-border crossing point used in the Soviet-era figures) and not flagged as a material disagreement, but I did not fill a Length ref since no source matches the value closely enough to responsibly pair with it.
